A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across pagination and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments across four visual decision domains and nine VLMs, human choice studies with 154 participants, and interpretability, mitigation, and distillation results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds held-out distillation, category-specific distillation, a CVPO candidate-count ablation, and human identity-matching results.

M1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds a category-specific distillation variant that derives editing themes separately for each product category instead of pooling products. The core CVPO, VFD, VTG, normalization, and summarization algorithms remain unchanged; the one-candidate experiment varies an existing parameter.

E1.justification: The four datasets and agent-choice domains remain unchanged. Appendix G adds a distinct human identity-matching task, beyond the earlier preference judgments. The additional held-out images otherwise extend sampling within existing domains.

E2.justification: The new held-out distillation comparisons use original and zero-shot images as baselines (Figure 8 and Table 4), whereas the retained in-sample Figure 6 compares distilled images with zero-shot and final optimized images. The VTG/VFD/CVPO comparison lineup remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds substantive evaluation designs: distillation on 20 new base images per task, category-specific product distillation, and CVPO evaluation with one candidate rather than three. Appendix G introduces matching of all 400 original/CVPO-final pairs in ten-pair sets, with two matchings per pair. These supplement rather than replace the existing protocols.

E4.justification: New Appendices E–G test generalization beyond optimization images, whether product-category heterogeneity explains distillation failure, whether CVPO's advantage survives fewer image proposals, and whether edited identities remain recognizable. These substantially extend validation beyond v1's existing distillation and mitigation analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix G adds a participant-level binomial GLM relating matching accuracy to task duration, with a confidence interval for the odds association. Existing cluster-robust linear probability models and uncertainty-reporting practices are retained. Neither version reports optimizer seed replication.

E6.justification: v2 adds held-out results favoring distillation over zero-shot editing in three of four domains. Table 4 reports category-specific product choice estimates of 35.9%, 55.9%, and 59.2% for original, zero-shot, and distilled images. The k=1 experiment retains CVPO's lead over VFD and reports 17.9 mean rounds; Appendix G reports 11 of 400 pairs mismatched by both raters. Existing numerical results are retained.

T1.justification: The latent-utility formulation, pairwise preference model, identity-maintenance definition, and optimization and equilibrium reasoning in Section 3.2 are unchanged. The added identity study supplies empirical validation, not a revised definition or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, seven introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same substantive claims about visual sensitivities, optimization, human preferences, interpretability, and partial mitigation. New appendix evidence supports these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v1 tentatively attributes product distillation failure to category heterogeneity; v2 claims corroboration and says category-specific distillation fixes it. Section 4.6 also extends the interpretation to unseen images. Appendix G attributes some matching failures to similar source images rather than optimization. The main limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F explicitly identifies the original three-candidate setting and the one-proposal-per-round ablation after initialization. The first-page project address changes from the Vercel address to sahaslab.com/visualpersuasion. Existing algorithm and prompt documentation is retained, and both conclusions still describe code and data release as forthcoming.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work positioning are unchanged. Reference-list differences are attributable to layout rather than additions or removals.

P1.justification: v2 inserts three appendix sections and updates cross-references, with limited additions to the main discussion. It also adds equal-contribution and conference-publication text. Most existing prose and the main section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 8–9 and Table 4, adjusts Figure 2's proportions, and resizes or repositions several retained displays. Some captions now specify the 50% base rate. Existing appendix displays are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The held-out tests, one-candidate ablation, and identity-matching study provide useful checks on weaknesses left largely untested in v1. Their value is bounded: Table 4's 59.2% versus 55.9% contrast has p≈0.1 despite the claim that category grouping fixes the problem, and successful identity matching does not establish that all substantive qualities remained unchanged. The additional validation nevertheless supports a limited overall improvement.
